You are not doing their work for them, only giving them the frame. When they can walk through what you saw with you nowhere around explaining, it has carried somewhere without you.
1.sheetLine: You see the shape. Now leave it where they can stand.

2.tense: You will keep gathering until it is certain, and it will not be certain.
2.verb: knowing what to attend to
2.place: seeing the whole pattern
2.ask: Pick what you are truly steering toward right now — the honest answer, not the safest — and turn toward it, dropping everything you have gathered that is not aiming there.
2.core:
The assembling has grown past what seeing needs. You keep adding angles, more evidence, more of the shape, and the shape gets larger without getting clearer, until standing back far enough to take all of it in puts you nowhere near the thing itself. The gathering is no longer serving you.

What would come back is a plain wanting, pointed. Not a strategy — the thing you would be sorriest to lose. Face it, in your own words, and steer by it. Then let everything you have collected that is not aiming there drop away, and take a small step toward what remains. Perceiving the shape is not the destination by itself; it is for walking toward something.
2.sheetLine: You gathered the whole map and stopped walking.

3.tense: You stood at a door that closed behind you, waiting for someone to open it.
3.ask: Choose one step you have been holding — the one whose ending you cannot already see — and take it, letting clarity arrive afterward rather than before.
3.core:
Standing here, your own read of a thing arrives and it does not get used. Instead you go looking for someone else to confirm it, and the confirmation keeps not quite coming, because no one sees what you see. Fog is filling the space where your own sense of a thing used to stand.

What you can do is smaller than getting the sight back — it is just taking one step while still unsure. Choose one step you have been holding, the one whose ending you cannot already see, and take it, letting clarity arrive afterward. You do not need the whole road lit. The first steps are mostly memory, and you have walked this far already.
3.sheetLine: Light comes after the step, not before it.

4.tense: You are already writing in this room, and your hand is off the pen.
4.verb: knowing what to attend to
4.place: seeing the whole pattern
4.ask: Take one decision from this month you shrugged off as a hunch and trace it back to what you spotted first — that credit is yours, and only you can return it.
4.core:
Decisions keep turning out well in ways you did not plan. You call a move a guess, and it turns out to be the right one. Somewhere in you the read is happening — clean, accurate, arriving before the reasons — and the part of you that takes credit for the outcome is not the part that did the spotting.

What is wanted here is credit given where it is due, without keeping a ledger. Pick one decision from the last month that went well and you shrugged off, and trace it back to what you actually noticed before you made it. That is not bragging; it is fair return on something you have been loaning out at no cost. Do it once and you will start catching the sight before it surprises you.
4.sheetLine: The sight is yours. Start signing for it.

1.tense: You are here at the crossing, and your read of the room holds.
1.verb: seeing what matters before you can say why
1.place: the threshold where something is finished and the next thing is already beginning
1.ask: Take a clear call you made this week and give it one home — a note, a folder, a place you will pass again. Small enough to keep, solid enough to return to.
1.core:
You are at the end of something, and the way you take a room in does not need defending. You catch the shape of it before you can explain how. Arriving early is ordinary to you, which is why you lean on it. You can sit with an unsolved question and not flinch, and that ease is what lets a completion open instead of close.
What comes next is a shape, not a push. Take one clear perception and give it a small form you can return to. The form serves what it carries. You are not building a cage; you are making room. Things make sense in your presence because you keep the edges clear.
1.sheetLine: You see it, and it holds.

2.tense: You are bracing toward a future you cannot write yet, and the volume keeps rising.
2.verb: seeing what matters before you can say why
2.place: the threshold where something is finished and the next thing is already beginning
2.ask: Of everything you are carrying right now, choose the thing you would miss most if it went. Turn and face that. The rest can stay where it is.
2.core:
At the crossing, more and more comes in. Every perception feels load-bearing, so nothing gets set down. You check a thing against itself, then against someone else's version, then against tomorrow's. What used to let you see through has thickened into a wall, and you are standing on the wrong side of it, waiting for a certainty that does not arrive. This is not knowing too much. It is refusing to choose what matters most.
There is a direction you can feel. Name the thing you would miss most, and face that. Not the whole map, not the plan — just the point you turn toward. Wanting it plainly will not cost you the rest. You do not need a wall to keep what matters; one line to steer by will do.
2.sheetLine: You are guarding everything, so nothing can move.

3.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you, asking others to read the sign.
3.verb: seeing what matters before you can say why
3.place: the threshold where something is finished and the next thing is already beginning
3.ask: Take a page and mark your situation roughly — no order, no polish, no explanation. Keep the page. Do not show anyone.
3.core:
The crossing happened, but you did not quite arrive on the other side. You keep looking for someone to confirm what you saw. The confusion is real, and it sits on top of something older — a way of taking a room in that you stopped trusting somewhere along the way. The clarity you find outside does not hold, because nothing you did not sign for will stay yours.
You do not need the whole picture. Take a page and mark it badly — where you are, what you carry, what you are leaving. No one has to see it. It will be rough and unfinished, and that is the point. You are not forcing clarity; you are giving the fog an edge to move against. Keep the page. It will be more honest than the answer you are asking for.
3.sheetLine: It is still yours. You stopped signing for it.

4.tense: You are writing in a room you do not remember entering, pen down but ink still moving.
4.verb: seeing what matters before you can say why
4.place: the threshold where something is finished and the next thing is already beginning
4.ask: Look back at one exchange from this week. Note what you gave and what came back. If it ran one way, settle it once — return a thing or reclaim one. Then leave it alone.
4.core:
The reading of rooms is operating, but you are not credited on it. Choices feel random because the perception moved through before you looked up. A hunch, you say, or luck, or a thing that turned out fine. But the hunches keep landing, and the decisions shaped by them have your name on them, even when you say they do not.
Bring it into the open by checking one exchange. Look at what moved between you and someone else recently — what you handed over, what came back. If it is out of proportion, adjust it once, plainly. Then stop. That is fairness, not punishment. Naming what moved is how the one who decided steps back beside the act.
4.sheetLine: The insight is yours. You keep filing it as chance.
